title: Introduction to CLI Development knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which approach best supports reliable work with Introduction to CLI Development?
options: Validate arguments before acting, print useful usage and errors, and choose meaningful exit codes.
Skip input validation because Node.js applications run on a trusted server.
Assume every supported runtime has identical APIs and scheduling behavior.
Store credentials and production secrets directly in the source file.
questions.answer_key: Validate arguments before acting, print useful usage and errors, and choose meaningful exit codes.
questions.explanation: Validate arguments before acting, print useful usage and errors, and choose meaningful exit codes. The example and verification steps should make this practice observable.

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under Introduction to CLI Development?
questions.explanation: “Types of command-line tools” is one of the subtopics retained from the supplied Node.js curriculum for this lesson.

questions.prompt: Before relying on a Introduction to CLI Development implementation, what verification is most useful?
options: Ignore failures so the program continues silently.
Use the same code regardless of documented version differences.
Verify the documented result in a supported runtime and test one failure or boundary case.
Assume the API behaves as expected without running a check.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result in a supported runtime and test one failure or boundary case.
questions.explanation: A small deterministic check plus a failure/boundary case helps distinguish a correct design from a happy-path-only example.
